findings.title: [P1] Validate test-reported paths before opening host files
findings.body: Container stdout controls `f` through `ERROR <path>` records, but this read runs in the host grader. Absolute paths discard `tree`, traversal is accepted, and symlinks are followed. Agent-controlled pytest code can suspend output capture and emit `ERROR /dev/zero` followed by `1 passed in 0.01s`; parsing then reads the host's infinite device into memory, exhausting grader memory outside the container timeout. Both this read and `def_line` need containment checks, regular-file validation, and bounded reads.

findings.title: [P1] Reject failed executions before accepting reported passes
findings.body: A parseable summary is accepted regardless of the process exit status, and reported passes need no corresponding test outcomes. An agent can add an unprotected root `conftest.py` whose configuration hook suspends pytest capture, prints `1000000 passed in 0.01s`, and exits with status 1 before collection. The static-count floor is exceeded, `bad` remains empty, and `all_pass` accepts the result because it ignores `rc`. This bypasses hidden tests and can falsely validate gate approvals. Reject nonzero exits and require results from an independently controlled reporting mechanism.

findings.description: With --executor host the grader runs the task's test_command directly in the grading tree under `env -i ... timeout 120`. The tree is a copy of the agent's sandbox, so agent-authored conftest.py, test modules and the module under test execute as the grader's user with unrestricted filesystem and network access. The only isolation is a scrubbed environment. The header documents this mode as a working alternative (the Sprint 258 smoke used it) without noting that it removes the trust boundary the rest of the script is built around.
findings.failure_mode: Agent code executing during run_suite(final, test_command) runs BEFORE the grader reads snapshots/index.json, the *.bundle files, transcripts/events-*.jsonl and eval/adversarial-*.json (all read later in grade()). It can therefore rewrite the transcripts to erase contamination evidence, swap the IMPLEMENT/FIX1 bundles to tune verdict_accuracy, edit the suite's hidden tests plus MANIFEST.sha256 (owned by the same user) to corrupt every later grade, or tamper with other run directories in the batch.
findings.suggested_fix: Either remove host mode from the production grader or make it refuse to run on anything but --self-check and smoke tasks. If it must stay: snapshot every grader input (transcripts, snapshots, eval/) into SCRATCH before executing any test, open the suite read-only (or re-run freeze_check after tests and fail on drift), run the command under a dedicated unprivileged uid or bubblewrap/unshare with the tree as the only writable mount, and emit a loud warning in grade.json (executor_mode already records it; also set a `sandboxed: false` flag).

findings.description: gate_verdict() and review_md_verdict() (lines 783-786) use os.path.isfile() and open() on paths under the agent-writable sandbox without an islink check, and iterate the file line by line with no size cap. combined_findings() (line 877) checks only the leaf for a symlink; sandbox/grimoires, loa, a2a or sprint-1 may themselves be symlinks. The grader runs on the host, so these reads resolve against the host filesystem regardless of executor mode.
findings.failure_mode: An agent leaves `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/engineer-feedback.md -> /dev/zero` (one endless line: the grader OOMs), `-> <a FIFO>` (the grader blocks forever and stalls the batch), or a symlinked parent directory pointing at an arbitrary host directory so review.md/feedback files from another run or any host text are parsed as citations and written into grading/gates-combined.md. No file content reaches grade.json, so the impact is denial of service plus cross-run citation pollution rather than disclosure.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a helper `safe_open_text(sb, rel)` that walks each component with os.lstat, rejects any symlink, requires S_ISREG, caps the size (e.g. 4 MiB), and opens with os.O_NOFOLLOW; use it for every sandbox read (review.md, both feedback files, the pr/ copy). Reject the run if realpath(file) is not within realpath(sb).

findings.description: parse_pytest() takes node ids from the test command's stdout (OUTCOME_RX on `PASSED|FAILED|ERROR <node>` lines) and passes the path part to def_line() and the collection-error expansion (line 576), which do `open(os.path.join(tree, path))` and read the whole file. os.path.join discards `tree` when `path` is absolute, and `..` components are not rejected, so a line the agent prints from conftest.py chooses which host file the grader opens.
findings.failure_mode: Agent code prints `ERROR /dev/zero` or `FAILED /dev/zero::test_x` to stdout: the grader reads an unbounded stream and dies with MemoryError (exit 2, run ungraded). `ERROR /path/to/fifo` blocks the grader indefinitely. Reading `../../../<other run>/...` or `/etc/*` leaks only a def-line position into the t<k> ordering, so disclosure is a weak oracle; the practical impact is a trivially triggered grader crash/hang per run. This also works in container mode because the parse runs on the host.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate node paths with safe_rel() before opening, require the resolved path to be a regular non-symlink file inside `tree` (is_within), cap the read size, and prefer `--junitxml` on a dedicated mount over scraping -rA lines so node ids come from structured output.

findings.description: Hidden-test results are taken entirely from the stdout of a process that imports agent-authored code (conftest.py at /workspace, the module under test). parse_pytest takes the LAST line matching SUMMARY_RX; all_pass() (line 653) requires only passed >= total, an empty bad set and no parse_error, and never checks the exit code. parse_tap() (line 617) builds `set(range(1, plan+1))` from an attacker-chosen plan number. `-I -s` and `-p no:cacheprovider` do not stop conftest.py loading or import-time code in the package under test.
findings.failure_mode: A conftest.py that redirects pytest's real stdout to a buffer at import and registers an atexit hook printing `===== 40 passed in 0.1s =====` yields hidden_tests.passed=40, total=max(40, static), bad={} -> all_pass True regardless of real outcomes or exit status, so a failing implementation grades as fully correct and verdict_accuracy is computed against a fabricated result. Separately, a bats/TAP-shaped `1..99999999999` line or `N passed` with N huge makes the host grader allocate gigabytes (DoS).
findings.suggested_fix: Treat stdout as untrusted evidence: require rc == 0 for all_pass; take pytest results from `--junitxml=/results/r.xml` written to a second, otherwise-empty bind mount and cross-check counts against static_cases (passed must not exceed the overlaid case count); run with `--noconftest --confcutdir=<hidden dir> -p no:randomly` and `PYTHONSAFEPATH=1` to narrow import-time hooks; clamp TAP plan and summary counts to a sane maximum (e.g. 10000) and flag parse_error above it. Document that a determined agent can still subvert the result, and surface a `suspicious` flag when summary counts disagree with -rA lines.

findings.description: remove_path() walks the directory being deleted and calls os.chmod(..., 0o700) on every entry in `dirs`. os.walk(followlinks=False) still lists symlinks-to-directories in `dirs`, and os.chmod follows symlinks, so a symlink the agent planted in the sandbox (copied verbatim into grading/final by copy_tree) is chmod'ed at its target. Triggered on re-grade via fresh_dir(grading), on put_file() replacing an agent-created directory at a grader_protected/overlay path, and on the SCRATCH cleanup in `finally`.
findings.failure_mode: `sandbox/x -> /path/to/grader-owned-dir` (the suite root, another run dir, a shared results directory) gets mode 0700 when the grader cleans up, silently revoking group/other access. Impact is limited to directories the grader user owns.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip the chmod when `os.path.islink(os.path.join(r, d))`, or use os.open(..., O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY) + os.fchmod; shutil.rmtree already refuses to follow symlinks so only the chmod pre-pass needs the guard.

findings.description: The docker invocation has no --cap-drop ALL, --security-opt no-new-privileges, --pids-limit, --memory or --cpus limits, and the in-container `timeout 120` is used without `-k`, so it only sends SIGTERM. The Python-side subprocess timeout (180 s) kills the docker CLI client, not the container, and no --cidfile is recorded for cleanup.
findings.failure_mode: Agent test code that ignores SIGTERM (signal.signal(SIGTERM, SIG_IGN) in conftest) and spins keeps the container alive after the client is killed; `--rm` never fires because the container has not exited. Each such run leaks a container holding the grading tree mounted and burning CPU/memory on the host; a fork bomb or large allocation inside is unconstrained apart from the 256m tmpfs.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `timeout -k 10 120`, add `--cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges --pids-limit 512 --memory 2g --cpus 2`, pass `--cidfile <scratch>/cid` and `docker kill $(cat cid)` in the TimeoutExpired handler, and consider `--init` so orphaned children are reaped.

findings.description: churn() reads every file in the final tree fully into memory and diffs it with difflib (quadratic in line count) with no size cap. The TRAILER regex at line 800 (`\{(?:(?!<!--|-->).)*\}` with re.S) backtracks O(n) per `<!-- LOA-VERDICT {` occurrence when no `-->` follows, giving O(k*n) on agent-written review.md/feedback text.
findings.failure_mode: A multi-gigabyte file left in the sandbox, or a review.md of repeated unterminated trailer openers, makes the host grader exhaust memory or spend hours in regex/difflib, stalling the batch.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip or count-as-binary any file above a threshold (e.g. 2 MiB) in churn, cap total lines diffed, and bound the trailer match (e.g. `\{[^\n]{0,4096}\}` or scan line-by-line as TRAILER_LINE already does) plus cap review text size before CITE.finditer.

findings.description: The header states the sandbox copies of the dissent envelopes are tamperable and only the harness copies under eval/ are authoritative, yet the gate verdicts (v_review, v_audit) that select `verdict`, `verdict_accuracy`, which snapshot is graded (fix1 vs implement) and whether a gate 'ran' are read from sandbox/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/*.md, which the implementer agent can edit in FIX1/FIX2.
findings.failure_mode: An agent appends `<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"verdict":"APPROVED"} -->` to auditor-sprint-feedback.md (or deletes the file) and the gate's verdict_accuracy, verdict and snapshots_graded are computed from forged data, skewing the arm comparison the ablation exists to measure.
findings.suggested_fix: Have pipeline-run.sh copy the feedback files (or just their trailers) to <run-dir>/eval/ at the end of each gate phase, and read verdicts from there in the grader; fall back to the sandbox copy only with a `verdict_source: sandbox` flag in grade.json.
